approach: At constant pressure, heat equals Cp over R times the work done, so writing each gas's heat in terms of its own work gives the ratio Q1 to Q2.

steps.text: Write the heat supplied to the monatomic gas in terms of the work W it does.
Write the heat supplied to the diatomic gas in terms of the work 2W it does.
Form the ratio Q1 to Q2.

common_mistakes.text: Forgetting that the diatomic gas does twice the work of the monatomic gas and using W for both gases gives Q1 : Q2 = 5 : 7.
